Apple___Apple_scab.summary: Fungal disease causing dark, scabby lesions on leaves and fruit.
steps: Remove and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to reduce spore sources.
Apply a protectant fungicide (e.g. captan or myclobutanil) starting at bud break.
Choose scab-resistant apple varieties for new plantings.

Apple___Black_rot.summary: Fungal disease causing leaf spots, fruit rot, and cankers on branches.
steps: Prune out dead or cankered wood during dormant season.
Remove mummified fruit left on the tree or ground.
Apply fungicide sprays during the growing season if pressure is high.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.summary: Fungal disease requiring both apple and cedar/juniper hosts to complete its cycle.
steps: Remove nearby cedar/juniper hosts where practical.
Apply fungicide from pink bud stage through several weeks after petal fall.
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties.
Continue regular monitoring and good orchard hygiene.
Continue regular monitoring and maintain proper soil pH (4.5-5.5).

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.summary: Fungal disease causing white powdery coating on leaves and shoots.
steps: Improve air circulation via pruning.
Apply sulfur-based or other labeled fungicides at first sign of disease.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization, which promotes susceptible new growth.
Continue regular monitoring.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.summary: Fungal disease causing rectangular gray-brown lesions on leaves.
steps: Rotate crops away from corn for at least one season.
Use resistant hybrids where available.
Apply foliar fungicide if disease appears before tasseling in susceptible fields.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.summary: Fungal disease causing reddish-brown pustules on leaves.
steps: Plant rust-resistant hybrids.
Apply fungicide if rust appears early and conditions favor spread (cool, humid).
Monitor fields regularly during the growing season.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.summary: Fungal disease causing long, cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on leaves.
steps: Rotate crops and till under residue to reduce spore survival.
Plant resistant hybrids.
Apply fungicide if detected early in susceptible fields, especially before tasseling.
Continue regular monitoring.

Grape___Black_rot.summary: Fungal disease causing brown leaf spots and shriveled, mummified fruit.
steps: Remove mummified berries and infected canes during pruning.
Apply fungicide from early shoot growth through fruit ripening.
Improve canopy airflow via proper vine training.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).summary: Fungal trunk disease causing striped leaf discoloration and berry spotting.
steps: Prune out and destroy infected wood; avoid pruning during wet weather.
Protect pruning wounds with a wound sealant/fungicide.
No fully curative treatment exists - focus on prevention and vine stress reduction.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.summary: Fungal disease causing angular brown leaf spots.
steps: Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves.
Apply labeled fungicide during humid periods.
Improve canopy airflow via pruning and trellising.
Continue regular monitoring.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).summary: Bacterial disease spread by psyllid insects; currently incurable.
steps: Remove and destroy infected trees to prevent spread.
Control Asian citrus psyllid populations with approved insecticides.
Source certified disease-free nursery stock for new plantings.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial disease causing small dark spots on leaves and fruit.
steps: Plant resistant peach varieties where available.
Apply copper-based bactericide sprays during dormant and early growing season.
Avoid overhead irrigation which spreads bacteria.
Continue regular monitoring.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial disease causing dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit.
steps: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Apply copper-based bactericide, ideally combined with mancozeb.
Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet.
Continue regular monitoring.

Potato___Early_blight.summary: Fungal disease causing dark concentric-ring spots on lower leaves.
steps: Rotate crops with non-solanaceous plants for 2+ years.
Apply fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or mancozeb) at first sign of disease.
Ensure adequate plant nutrition, especially nitrogen, to reduce susceptibility.

Potato___Late_blight.summary: Fast-spreading fungal-like disease (Phytophthora) causing dark lesions; historically caused the Irish famine.
steps: Apply fungicide preventatively during cool, wet weather.
Destroy volunteer potato plants and cull piles that can harbor the pathogen.
Use certified disease-free seed potatoes.
Continue regular monitoring.
Continue regular monitoring.
Continue regular monitoring.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.summary: Fungal disease causing white powdery patches on leaves.
steps: Space plants for good air circulation.
Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, or other labeled fungicide at first sign.
Choose resistant varieties where available.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.summary: Fungal disease causing purplish spots that merge into scorched-looking leaves.
steps: Remove infected leaves after harvest.
Apply labeled fungicide during wet periods.
Ensure good bed spacing and airflow.
Continue regular monitoring.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial disease causing small dark spots on leaves, stems, and fruit.
steps: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Apply copper-based bactericide; rotate with non-solanaceous crops.
Avoid overhead watering and working with wet plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.summary: Fungal disease causing concentric-ring spots on older leaves first.
steps: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves.
Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or mancozeb) at first sign.
Mulch to prevent soil splash onto leaves, and rotate crops.

Tomato___Late_blight.summary: Fast-spreading disease that can destroy a crop within days in cool, wet weather.
steps: Apply fungicide preventatively when conditions favor disease (cool, humid).
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately to limit spread.
Avoid overhead irrigation and improve airflow between plants.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.summary: Fungal disease common in humid greenhouse conditions, causing yellow spots and moldy leaf undersides.
steps: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity around plants.
Apply labeled fungicide if conditions remain favorable for disease.
Space and prune plants for better airflow.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.summary: Fungal disease causing many small circular spots with dark borders.
steps: Remove infected lower leaves promptly.
Apply fungicide at first sign and repeat per label interval.
Mulch and avoid overhead watering to reduce splash spread.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.summary: Pest damage (not a disease) causing stippled, bronzed leaves; mites thrive in hot, dry conditions.
steps: Spray plants with water to dislodge mites, or apply insecticidal soap/miticide.
Introduce natural predators (e.g. predatory mites) where feasible.
Avoid excess dust and drought stress, which favor mite outbreaks.

Tomato___Target_Spot.summary: Fungal disease causing brown lesions with concentric rings, similar to early blight.
steps: Remove infected plant debris after harvest.
Apply labeled fungicide at first sign of disease.
Improve airflow through proper spacing and pruning.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.summary: Viral disease spread by whiteflies, causing yellowing, curling leaves and stunted growth.
steps: Control whitefly populations with insecticides or reflective mulches.
Remove and destroy infected plants to reduce virus reservoirs.
Use virus-resistant tomato varieties where available.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.summary: Viral disease causing mottled light/dark green leaf patterns and stunted growth.
steps: Remove and destroy infected plants; the virus has no cure.
Disinfect tools between plants and wash hands after handling tobacco products (a related virus source).
Use resistant varieties and certified virus-free seed.
Continue regular monitoring.
